task.title: Transitive dependency memo invalidation
task.specification: Config deps is a finite DAG of existing nodes; values gives an integer for every leaf (empty dependency list). A nonleaf value is sum of its immediate dependency values; repeated dependencies are not present. Start empty memo. Events evaluate{node},set{node,value}. Set changes only a leaf; nonleaf set ignored. Successful set invalidates that leaf and every transitive dependent, even if value unchanged. Evaluate computes dependencies in their listed order, memoizes leaves and intermediate nodes, and returns the node value. Output {value:integer_or_null,computed:number of newly memoized nodes this event,valid:[sorted memoized node IDs]}. Set value=null and computed=0. Cached evaluate computed=0. No undefined nodes or cycles are supplied. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}, initially state=null. Only the current event is supplied; every named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"restore"}. Return exactly the stated output fields each step; opaque JSON state is not graded. All numeric inputs and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; time deltas are nonnegative. Unless a task explicitly overrides this, keys, snapshot IDs, readers and graph nodes are single lowercase ASCII letters. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. At most eight identities and 48 events occur. Configurations and event fields shown below are present. Ordinary regimes use moderate storage and timing; boundary uses equality/empty states; adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events; shift uses smaller capacity, longer timing gaps or deeper dependency shapes, without changing these rules. Generator regimes: Boundary uses independent leaves; shift uses six DAG nodes versus four with randomly sampled acyclic dependencies. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Comparator hysteresis
matchedCard.relation: A state-dependent comparator uses distinct upper and lower transition thresholds. Between them, the existing state is retained. Fluctuations that remain within this interval need not cause repeated switching.
assumptions: The output has a preceding state.
Distinct thresholds are appropriate to the signal range and acceptable response delay.
matchedCard.boundary: A wider separation can postpone response to a real change. Behavior with two state-dependent thresholds differs from reacting to every crossing of one fixed threshold.
matchedCard.source_fact: Texas Instruments describes an inverting comparator with upper and lower hysteresis thresholds to reduce unwanted transitions caused by noise or slow-moving signals.

shuffledCard.label: Dendrochronology
shuffledCard.relation: Overlapping sequences can be aligned by distinctive patterns spanning several observations. Cross-comparison can reveal missing or extra local observations that a simple position count would treat as elapsed intervals.
assumptions: The sequences share a comparable underlying history.
The overlap contains enough distinguishing structure to support alignment.
shuffledCard.boundary: Repeated patterns or insufficient overlap can support several alignments. A single coincident observation does not establish a unique chronological match.
shuffledCard.source_fact: NOAA describes crossdating tree-ring patterns from several trees to account for missing or extra rings and align samples from different periods.

initial.explanation: The rule is direct: memoization is demand-driven, and setting a leaf invalidates exactly that leaf and all nodes reachable from it through reverse dependency edges. A set always returns null with zero newly computed nodes. Evaluation recursively follows listed dependency order, reusing valid memo entries.
initial.mapping: config.deps and config.values map node IDs to dependency lists and leaf values; state stores current leaf values and memoized node values; event.type selects evaluation or invalidation.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated finite-DAG, existing-node, safe-integer contract. State is only produced by this function.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let d=input.config.deps,v=input.config.values,m={};function inv(x){delete m[x];for(let k in d)if(d[k].indexOf(x)>=0)inv(k)}function ev(x){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(m,x))return m[x];let q=d[x],z;if(q.length===0)z=v[x];else{z=0;for(let i=0;i<q.length;i++)z+=ev(q[i])}m[x]=z;return z}for(let i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let e=input.events[i],o=output[i],c=0;if(e.type==='set'){if(d[e.node].length===0){v[e.node]=e.value;inv(e.node)}if(o.value!==null||o.computed!==0)return false}else{let before=Object.keys(m).length,z=ev(e.node),a=Object.keys(m).sort();if(o.value!==z||o.computed!==Object.keys(m).length-before||JSON.stringify(o.valid)!==JSON.stringify(a))return false}}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){const d=config.deps;let s=state;if(s===null){s={v:{},m:{}};for(const k in config.values)s.v[k]=config.values[k]}function drop(x){delete s.m[x];for(const k in d)if(d[k].indexOf(x)>=0)drop(k)}let computed=0,value=null;if(event.type==='set'){if(d[event.node].length===0){s.v[event.node]=event.value;drop(event.node)}}else{function get(x){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,x))return s.m[x];let q=d[x],z;if(q.length===0)z=s.v[x];else{z=0;for(let i=0;i<q.length;i++)z+=get(q[i])}s.m[x]=z;computed++;return z}value=get(event.node)}return{state:s,output:{value,computed,valid:Object.keys(s.m).sort()}}}

final.explanation: Memoization is demand-driven. Evaluation recursively visits dependencies in listed order, reuses valid memo entries, stores each newly computed node, and reports the number newly stored. Setting a leaf updates its value and invalidates that leaf plus every transitive dependent through reverse dependency traversal. Setting a nonleaf is ignored. Every set returns null and zero computed nodes.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){const d=config.deps;let s=state;if(s===null){s={v:{},m:{}};for(const k in config.values)s.v[k]=config.values[k]}function invalidate(x){delete s.m[x];for(const k in d)if(d[k].indexOf(x)!==-1)invalidate(k)}let value=null,computed=0;if(event.type==='set'){const x=event.node;if(d[x].length===0){s.v[x]=event.value;invalidate(x)}}else{function evalNode(x){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,x))return s.m[x];const q=d[x];let z;if(q.length===0)z=s.v[x];else{z=0;for(let i=0;i<q.length;i++)z+=evalNode(q[i])}s.m[x]=z;computed++;return z}value=evalNode(event.node)}return{state:s,output:{value:value,computed:computed,valid:Object.keys(s.m).sort()}}}

initial.explanation: Memoize each evaluated node. A leaf update invalidates that leaf and every node reachable from it through dependency edges; unrelated memoized nodes remain valid. Evaluation recursively follows listed dependency order and counts only newly memoized nodes.
initial.mapping: The memo table is the retained state; dependency reachability maps leaf changes to invalidated computed values.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated DAG, node, and safe-integer constraints. State is only produced by this program.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){var c=input.config, s={v:Object.assign({},c.values),m:{}}, want=[]; function inv(x){var q=[x],b={};while(q.length){var n=q.pop();if(b[n])continue;b[n]=1;for(var k in c.deps)if(c.deps[k].indexOf(n)>=0)q.push(k)}for(var k in b)delete s.m[k]} function ev(n){var count=0;function f(x){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,x))return s.m[x];var ds=c.deps[x],z;if(!ds.length)z=s.v[x];else{z=0;for(var i=0;i<ds.length;i++)z+=f(ds[i])}s.m[x]=z;count++;return z}var z=f(n),v=Object.keys(s.m).sort();return {value:z,computed:count,valid:v}}for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var e=input.events[i];if(e.type==='set'){if(c.deps[e.node].length===0){s.v[e.node]=e.value;inv(e.node)}want.push({value:null,computed:0,valid:Object.keys(s.m).sort()})}else want.push(ev(e.node))}return JSON.stringify(want)===JSON.stringify(output)}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){var s=state||{v:Object.assign({},config.values),m:{}};if(event.type==='set'){if(config.deps[event.node].length===0){s.v[event.node]=event.value;var q=[event.node],bad={};while(q.length){var n=q.pop();if(bad[n])continue;bad[n]=1;for(var k in config.deps)if(config.deps[k].indexOf(n)>=0)q.push(k)}for(var k in bad)delete s.m[k]}return {state:s,output:{value:null,computed:0,valid:Object.keys(s.m).sort()}}}var count=0;function f(n){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,n))return s.m[n];var d=config.deps[n],z;if(!d.length)z=s.v[n];else{z=0;for(var i=0;i<d.length;i++)z+=f(d[i])}s.m[n]=z;count++;return z}var value=f(event.node);return {state:s,output:{value:value,computed:count,valid:Object.keys(s.m).sort()}}}

final.explanation: The state stores current leaf values and memoized node values. Evaluation recursively processes dependencies in their listed order, reuses cached values, and counts only nodes newly memoized during that event. A successful leaf set invalidates the leaf and every transitive dependent; nonleaf sets are ignored. Outputs always contain the required value, computed count, and sorted valid memoized IDs.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){var s=state||{v:Object.assign({},config.values),m:{}};if(event.type==='set'){var n=event.node;if(config.deps[n].length===0){s.v[n]=event.value;var q=[n],bad={};while(q.length){var x=q.pop();if(bad[x])continue;bad[x]=1;for(var k in config.deps)if(config.deps[k].indexOf(x)>=0)q.push(k)}for(var k in bad)delete s.m[k]}return{state:s,output:{value:null,computed:0,valid:Object.keys(s.m).sort()}}}var count=0;function evalNode(n){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,n))return s.m[n];var d=config.deps[n],v;if(d.length===0)v=s.v[n];else{v=0;for(var i=0;i<d.length;i++)v+=evalNode(d[i])}s.m[n]=v;count++;return v}var value=evalNode(event.node);return{state:s,output:{value:value,computed:count,valid:Object.keys(s.m).sort()}}}

initial.explanation: Memoize each evaluated node. A leaf reads its current value; a nonleaf sums dependencies in listed order. Setting a leaf invalidates it and all reverse-reachable dependents, while setting a nonleaf does nothing.
initial.mapping: Nodes map to memo entries and reverse dependency reachability; leaf values map to current values, with configuration values as initial values.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated DAG, node, integer, and event constraints. State is retained exactly as returned between events.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(let i=0;i<output.length;i++){let o=output[i];if(!o||typeof o.value!=='number'&&o.value!==null||!Number.isInteger(o.computed)||!Array.isArray(o.valid)||o.valid.some(x=>typeof x!=='string'))return false}let n=input.events[0].node;return output[0].computed===1&&output[0].value===input.config.values[n]}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{m:{},v:{}};if(!s.m)s.m={};if(!s.v)s.v={};let d=config.deps, vals=config.values, type=event.type, node=event.node;let rev={};for(let k in d)rev[k]=[];for(let k in d)for(let x of d[k])rev[x].push(k);let out={value:null,computed:0,valid:[]};if(type==='set'){if(d[node].length===0){s.v[node]=event.value;let q=[node],seen={};while(q.length){let x=q.pop();if(seen[x])continue;seen[x]=1;delete s.m[x];for(let y of rev[x])q.push(y)}}}else if(type==='evaluate'){let made=0;function ev(x){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,x))return s.m[x];let z;if(d[x].length===0)z=Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.v,x)?s.v[x]:vals[x];else{z=0;for(let y of d[x])z+=ev(y)}s.m[x]=z;made++;return z}out.value=ev(node);out.computed=made}out.valid=Object.keys(s.m).sort();return{state:s,output:out}}

final.explanation: Maintains memoized node values and current leaf values in opaque state. Evaluation recursively processes dependencies in listed order, counting only newly memoized nodes. Setting a leaf updates its value and invalidates that leaf plus every reverse-reachable dependent; setting a nonleaf has no effect. Each output lists remaining memoized IDs in sorted order.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{m:{},v:{}};let d=config.deps,base=config.values,n=event.node,out={value:null,computed:0,valid:[]};if(event.type==='set'){if(d[n].length===0){s.v[n]=event.value;let r={};for(let k in d)r[k]=[];for(let k in d)for(let x of d[k])r[x].push(k);let q=[n];while(q.length){let x=q.pop();if(s.m[x]!==undefined||Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,x))delete s.m[x];for(let y of r[x])q.push(y)}}}else if(event.type==='evaluate'){let count=0;function get(x){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.m,x))return s.m[x];let z;if(d[x].length===0)z=Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.v,x)?s.v[x]:base[x];else{z=0;for(let y of d[x])z+=get(y)}s.m[x]=z;count++;return z}out.value=get(n);out.computed=count}out.valid=Object.keys(s.m).sort();return{state:s,output:out}}
